project.title: EviSeq: Source-Grounded Summarization with Composed Pretrained Encoders and Causal Decoders

contract.gap: A width-matching adapter does not specify how an independently pretrained encoder and causal decoder should allocate source information while preserving lexical evidence.
contract.task: Design and evaluate a full-memory source-grounded interface for long-document summarization.

questions.text: Does EviSeq reduce a source-unsupported-content signal relative to fine-tuned decoder-only LLMs on four datasets, operationalized by AlignScore consistency and H=1-C? A typed entity/number/relation error claim requires a separate adjudicated audit.

How does EviSeq affect ROUGE-1/2/L F1 and BERTScore-F1 relative to fine-tuned decoder-only controls and T5Gemma2 under matched records, budgets, preprocessing, and decoding, with native input serialization documented, on PubMed, ArXiv, BookSum, and GovReport?
Which of the encoder, AFMR bridge, and grounded-copy route contributes to the observed behavior under the registered decoder and training protocol?
Does the interface transfer across the registered causal and embedding encoders, and what quality/factuality differences are observed under their directionality and capacity confounds?

contract.contribution: A constrained full-memory interface and a reproducible four-question evaluation contract for composing pretrained encoder and decoder checkpoints; empirical gains remain pending.
nonclaims: No measured ROUGE or factuality improvement is claimed before the locked runs.
AFMR is not a factuality guarantee or calibrated hallucination probability.
The paper does not claim novelty for copied cross-attention, pointer generation, or generic pretrained model composition.

alignment.interpretation: PENDING; report as a proxy signal rather than a calibrated hallucination rate
alignment.limitation: AlignScore is a proxy and 1-AlignScore is not a calibrated probability

alignment.method: ROUGE-1/2/L F1 and BERTScore-F1 under matched records, budgets, preprocessing, decoding, and explicit native input serialization
alignment.evidence: Scorer-locked predictions and paired bootstrap intervals
alignment.limitation: Overlap and embedding metrics do not establish factual correctness

alignment.method: No-encoder, no-bridge, and no-grounded-copy component-contribution ablations with the same decoder and budget
alignment.evidence: Four-dataset ablation predictions and component diagnostics
alignment.limitation: Ablations can reveal necessity under the selected interface but not universal causality

alignment.method: Encoder-transfer matrix with PPLX, Qwen causal, Qwen embedding, and Nemotron embedding encoders
alignment.evidence: Matched training/evaluation runs and hidden-width/parameter reports
alignment.limitation: Encoder pretraining and directionality remain partly confounded
